Nolan Kido / Living Well

Free resources for a thoughtful ordinary life

A place to begin

Something worth your attention.

18 free starting points, not a list to finish.

Listen to a conversation, try a small practice, understand a tool, or find a book. Each selection explains why it belongs here and what you need before opening it.

All Living Well pages are free and need no account. Outside resources have their own access requirements, shown below. These are editorial selections, not a list of tools Nolan claims to have used.

Meaning, wonder & spiritual curiosity

A conversation, some context, or a bigger question. You do not need a new identity to begin.

Start with On Being: a conversation about attention when you would rather choose just one.

Listen or read · Free to browse

On Being: a conversation about attention

The On Being Project

A way into meaning through a person and a conversation rather than a list of conclusions. The selected interview connects creative work with attention to the world.

Begin here: Open the Mary Oliver conversation and choose audio or the transcript. You can begin with a short passage.

Access: Free web audio and transcript; no subscription needed for this selection.

Mary Oliver in conversation

Before you go

A personal conversation, not a universal spiritual teaching.

Related reading on Living Well

Religious traditions, with context

Harvard University, The Pluralism Project

Spiritual vocabulary means more when it is connected to the people and histories that use it. This collection helps provide that context.

Begin here: Read Rivers of Faith, then choose one tradition that you would like to understand better.

Access: Free public essays; no registration needed to read.

Rivers of Faith

Before you go

The project has an American context. Traditions are not interchangeable or internally uniform.

Related reading on Living Well

Public source reviewed 2026-10-09. Provider details. No claim of firsthand use or a completed course.

Read or explore · Free to browse

A landscape of consciousness

Closer To Truth

For a larger question after an ordinary one: how does felt experience relate to the world we can describe? This is an orientation to different proposed answers.

Begin here: Begin with Exploring Consciousness rather than trying to navigate the entire theory map.

Access: Free public introduction; no registration needed to read.

Exploring Consciousness

Before you go

This is a broad taxonomy, not a ranking of evidence or proof that all proposals are equally supported.

Related reading on Living Well

Public source reviewed 2026-10-09. Provider details. No claim of firsthand use or a completed course.

Attention & a less punishing inner life

Explore one optional practice. There is no course to finish and no ideal state to achieve.

Start with A brief guided pause when you would rather choose just one.

Listen or read · Free to browse

A brief guided pause

UCLA Mindful, UCLA Health

A straightforward starting point without needing another subscription. The recordings let you explore a practice rather than commit to an entire program.

Begin here: Find the three-minute Body and Sound Meditation in the English list, or choose a language and format that suits you.

Access: Free web audio; transcripts for some recordings. An app is optional.

UCLA guided recordings and transcripts

Before you go

An optional practice, not a treatment promise. Skip or stop anything uncomfortable; keep essential care and access needs intact.

Related reading on Living Well

Public source reviewed 2026-10-09. Provider details. No claim of firsthand use or a completed course.

Read and try · Free to browse

Awe Outing

Greater Good Science Center, UC Berkeley

A prompt for approaching familiar surroundings with curiosity. Its written format offers another way in besides guided audio.

Begin here: Read the instructions and choose an accessible setting that already fits your day.

Access: Free practice instructions; optional accounts support saving and participation.

Read the Awe Outing practice

Before you go

Keep necessary devices available despite the source's suggestion to put them away. No special feeling is required.

Related reading on Living Well

Practice in a named tradition

Plum Village App

An example of technology carrying a contemplative tradition. It belongs alongside, not in place of, secular and other spiritual approaches.

Begin here: Explore the public sample and background before deciding whether to install the app.

Plum Village app and sample audio

How AI Works

Code.org

Technology that returns you to the world

Notice something, borrow a book, and let the tool remain a small part of the experience.

Start with Seek by iNaturalist when you would rather choose just one.

App · Free app

Merlin Bird ID

Cornell Lab of Ornithology

A small way to connect an unfamiliar bird with a question you can investigate. The identification is the beginning of noticing, not the end.

Begin here: Read the official setup guide and check the identification support for your region.

Access: Free app; email confirmation is required for continued use. Download only through the official links.

Merlin setup and access guide

Before you go

Suggestions can be wrong, and Sound ID coverage varies by region. No credit card is required by Merlin.

Related reading on Living Well

Public source reviewed 2026-10-09. Provider details. No claim of firsthand use or a completed course.

App · Free app

Seek by iNaturalist

iNaturalist

Image recognition can help you ask better questions about something already nearby, rather than give you another reason to keep scrolling.

Begin here: Read about the app before installing. Try observing one thing without needing to collect badges.

Access: Free app; no registration required for basic use.

Learn about Seek

Before you go

Optional iNaturalist sign-in and posting change data sharing. Never use identification guesses to decide what is safe to eat or touch.

Related reading on Living Well

Public source reviewed 2026-10-09. Provider details. No claim of firsthand use or a completed course.

OverDrive and participating libraries

People, memory & showing up

Tools for listening, remembering, and making ordinary participation easier.

Start with A question for a real conversation when you would rather choose just one.

Read and talk · Free to browse

A question for a real conversation

StoryCorps

A useful starting point when you want to hear more from someone but do not know where to begin. The value can remain in the conversation itself.

Begin here: Choose one question from Great Questions for Anyone and ask whether the person would enjoy discussing it.

Access: Free public question bank. Recording or uploading is not required to use it.

Browse Great Questions

Before you go

Agreement to talk is not permission to record, upload, or publish. Skip intrusive questions.

Related reading on Living Well

How this is selected

Free does not mean identical access.

Free to browse means the selected public material can be read or opened without a paid plan. Free app may still require installation and setup. Free with an account requires registration. Library card required depends on your library and eligibility. A free course does not make every tool it demonstrates free.

Public provider pages and access information were reviewed on October 9, 2026. Apps have not been installed, courses have not been completed, and every media player or regional access path has not been tested. These are not security audits or personal testimonials. External sites have their own privacy practices.

The annotations are original; the linked work stays with its creators. There are no affiliate links in this collection. A free resource is not necessarily licensed for republication.

Sources behind our articles are kept separate from this browsing collection. Found a changed access requirement? Send a correction.
